To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dibutyryl cyclic AMP enhances the synthesis of Epstein-Barr viral (EBV) antigens and viral particles in hybrid cells induced by IUdR.

(i) the presence of B2-cAMP during the induction of EBV by IUdR increases the percentage of cells expressing EBV early antigens (EA) and viral capsid antigen (VCA); (ii) Bt2-cAMp reduces the time necessary for the appearance of EBV capsid particles; (iii) the effect is dose-dependent; (iv) Bt2cAMP induces EA and VCA in EBV negative hybrid cell lines; (v)
the incidence of cells producing EBV early and capsid antigens is increased in the presence of dibutyryl cyclic AMP and the time required for production of virus particles is reduced.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the synthesis of Epstein-Barr viral (EBV) antigens and virus capsids.
the induction of Epstein-Barr (EB) virus in somatic cell hybrids.
the effect of cyclic AMP and related compounds on the expression of the EBV genome in somatic cell hybrids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Bt2-cAM is an inducer of EBV expression in EBV negative somatic cell lines.

the effect of dibutyryl cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) on the induction of Epstein-Barr (EB) virus in somatic cell hybrids is to increase the incidence of cells expressing EBV early antigen and virus capsid antigen, to decrease the time required for the appearance of virus particles, and to induce EBV antigens in cells not exposed to 5′- iododeoxyuridine.
Bt2-camp is an effective inducer of EBV in EBV negative hybrid cell lines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of B2-cAMP enhances EBV induction in somatic cell hybrids.
Bt2-cAMp enhances the expression of latent EBV genome in hybrid cells.
Bt2-cAMp enhances the induction and expression of EBV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cAMP may act to regulate the synthesis of viral antigens and virus capsid proteins in the hybrid cell system, and may be involved in the regulation of the expression of the EBV genome.
the concentration of intracellular cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) may be one of the control factors selecting for gene expression.

the presence of Btu2-cAMP during induction with IUdR increases the incidence of cells expressing EBV early and capsid antigens and reduces the time necessary for appearance and maturation of EBV particles.
